building_footprints.title: building footprints
building_footprints.method: Overture's conflated footprints (OSM, Google Open Buildings, Microsoft). Traced and machine-detected shapes are mixed, so the layer is shown as modelled, the weaker of the two.

building_heights.title: building heights
building_heights.method: Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal heights (4 m effective, latest year) where Earth Engine is set up, else GHS-BUILT-H's average net building height (about 90 m, 2018); the mean over pixels with a building, so empty ground does not pull a unit down.

city_boundary.title: city boundary
city_boundary.method: The union of the city's wards, so the city is exactly the area its wards cover.

density.title: density
density.method: People divided by land area (water excluded), computed again from the sums at each unit.

land_cover.title: land cover
land_cover.method: ESA WorldCover classes at 10 m, as each class's share of every grid cell and ward.

lst_hot_season.title: land surface temperature, hot season
lst_hot_season.method: Median of clear Landsat 8/9 C2 L2 surface-temperature scenes in the hot months of the chosen years; QA bits 0 to 5 masked; ST_QA uncertainty over 5 K dropped. Surface, not air.

night_lights.title: night lights
night_lights.method: VIIRS annual radiance (NASA Black Marble, near-nadir, snow-free), the mean per cell and ward; measured light, used only as a proxy for activity.

population.title: people
population.method: Modelled population per 30 m pixel (census counts spread over detected buildings), summed to the 150 m grid and to wards.

space_syntax.title: space syntax (integration and choice)
space_syntax.method: Angular segment analysis on the walkable streets. City-wide: NAIN and NACH at 2 km, exact from every segment; NAIN at n, estimated from 400 random origins (angular depth is symmetric, so their depths give every segment an unbiased estimate of its total depth). The window computes 400 m and 800 m live. Cells and wards take the mean of the segments whose middles fall in them.

streets.title: streets
streets.method: The roads and paths a person can walk (every class but motorways), from Overture's segments of OpenStreetMap. On the grid and wards: metres of street per hectare of the unit's land in the city.

surface_water.title: surface water
surface_water.method: JRC Global Surface Water occurrence: the share of valid observations from 1984 to 2020 in which each 30 m pixel was water, as the mean per cell and ward.

terrain_bare_earth.title: ground (bare earth)
terrain_bare_earth.method: FABDEM, Copernicus GLO-30 with buildings and trees removed by a model; under the commercial setting the surface model stands in, and drainage reads worse.

terrain_surface.title: ground and roofs (surface)
terrain_surface.method: Copernicus GLO-30 heights, which include buildings and trees.

wards.title: wards
wards.method: The city's ward polygons from the first open source that covers it, with the delimitation year on the card. Properties are renamed to ward_id, ward_no and name; nothing is redrawn.

bhuvan_lulc.title: Bhuvan land use and land cover, 1:50k
bhuvan_lulc.reliability_note: Shown as WMS in the atlas only; no export, nothing derived published (single-user, non-transferable licence).
bhuvan_lulc.citation: Bhuvan terms of use (as quoted 2015; current wording to re-read)

black_marble.title: NASA Black Marble, annual night lights (VNP46A4, collection 2)
black_marble.licence: NASA open data (no restrictions on use)
black_marble.reliability_note: Corrected for moonlight, atmosphere, snow and seasonal vegetation, which VNL is not. The near-nadir snow-free composite is used, since off-nadir views see building walls and read brighter in dense cores. Downloads need a free NASA Earthdata login.
black_marble.citation: Román et al. 2018, Remote Sensing of Environment 210, 113-143
black_marble.attribution: NASA Black Marble VNP46A4 (Román et al. 2018), LAADS DAAC

cartodem.title: CartoDEM
cartodem.reliability_note: Dropped as a candidate: private users need ISRO clearance, and Bhuvan's licence is single-user and non-transferable, so nothing derived from it could be published.
cartodem.citation: Bhuvan terms of use (as quoted 2015; current wording to re-read)

copernicus_glo30.title: Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (surface)
copernicus_glo30.attribution: Copernicus DEM, © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018, provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA

datameet_wards.title: Municipal Spatial Data (ward boundaries)
datameet_wards.reliability_note: Bengaluru's BBMP.geojson is the 243 wards of the 2022 delimitation, scraped from KSRSAC's Bengaluru GIS. The city has since become five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (about 369 wards, 2025); those boundaries are not yet open as GIS (phase B9).
datameet_wards.attribution: Municipal Spatial Data by DataMeet India community (CC BY 4.0)

dynamic_world.title: Dynamic World (annual composite)
dynamic_world.attribution: Dynamic World, Google and WRI (Brown et al. 2022), CC BY 4.0

esa_worldcover.title: ESA WorldCover 2021
esa_worldcover.attribution: © ESA WorldCover project 2021 / contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2021), CC BY 4.0

fabdem.title: FABDEM (forest and buildings removed Copernicus DEM)
fabdem.attribution: FABDEM, Hawker et al. (2022), CC BY-NC-SA 4.0

ghs_built_h.title: GHS-BUILT-H R2023A (average net building height, 3 arc-seconds)
ghs_built_h.attribution: GHSL, European Commission JRC (2023), CC BY 4.0

ghs_pop.title: GHS-POP R2023A (residential population, 2020, 3 arc-seconds)
ghs_pop.attribution: GHSL, European Commission JRC (2023), GHS-POP R2023A, CC BY 4.0

jrc_gsw.title: JRC Global Surface Water v1.3
jrc_gsw.licence: Copernicus programme terms (free, with acknowledgement and citation)
jrc_gsw.attribution: Source EC JRC/Google (Pekel et al. 2016, Nature)

landsat_c2_l2_st.title: Landsat 8/9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature
landsat_c2_l2_st.reliability_note: Thermal band about 100 m, resampled to 30 m by USGS. Surface temperature, not air.
landsat_c2_l2_st.attribution: Landsat imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey

meta_hrsl.title: High Resolution Settlement Layer v1.5
meta_hrsl.attribution: Data for Good at Meta and CIESIN, High Resolution Settlement Layer (CC BY 4.0)

open_buildings_25d.title: Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal
open_buildings_25d.reliability_note: 4 m effective (rasters at 0.5 m) from Sentinel-2; covers Africa, South and South-East Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, so all pilots including Dhaka.
open_buildings_25d.attribution: Google Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal, CC BY 4.0

opencity_wards.title: Ward boundaries (OpenCity)
opencity_wards.reliability_note: Delhi MCD 2022 (250 wards) and Guwahati 2022 (credited to Esri India's Living Atlas), as KML.

overture_buildings.title: Overture Maps buildings
overture_buildings.reliability_note: Conflated from OSM, Google Open Buildings and Microsoft footprints; traced and ML-detected shapes mixed.

overture_transportation.title: Overture Maps transportation segments
overture_transportation.reliability_note: OpenStreetMap's roads and paths, cut by Overture into segments between connectors; read as GeoParquet with DuckDB.

viirs_vnl.title: VIIRS Nighttime Lights, annual (VNL v2)
viirs_vnl.publisher: Earth Observation Group, Colorado School of Mines
viirs_vnl.reliability_note: Dropped as a candidate (2026-10-26): EOG now releases VNL under licence only, and scripted access has been for paid subscribers since June 2026. NASA Black Marble stands in.
viirs_vnl.attribution: Earth Observation Group, Payne Institute, Colorado School of Mines (Elvidge et al. 2021), CC BY 4.0
